answer:
Based on the Our World in Data page "Wars ranked by death toll, 1800-2011," here are the **top four interstate wars** between 1800 and 2011 that caused the most combatant deaths:

| Rank | War | Combatant Deaths |
|------|-----|------------------|
| 1 | **World War II** | 21.1 million |
| 2 | **World War I** | 7.11 million |
| 3 | **Second Sino-Japanese War** | 1.69 million |
| 4 | **Vietnam War** | 1.06 million |

These figures represent deaths of combatants due to fighting in conventional wars. Note that some other major conflicts appearing just below this threshold include the Chinese Civil War (1.2M), which is excluded from this list because it was an intrastate/civil war rather than an interstate conflict.
